01_docstring_closer_then_code.py.why: A1: a lone docstring closer opened a fake docstring that swallowed code; the # pair moved past the asserts

02_docstring_zh_continuation.py.why: A3: Chinese continuation lines with only identifiers and full-width punctuation were classified as English

03_comment_zh_continuation.py.why: A3: same, inside a # comment block

04_comment_then_code.py.why: A5: the comment block ran on into real code and was flagged as commented-out code

05_zh_with_identifier.py.why: A6: a Chinese sentence with an identifier is not a mixed-language line

06_no_separator.py.why: B10: multi-line EN directly followed by multi-line ZH must be flagged, not fixed

08_mid_sentence_blank.py.why: A7: a blank line inside a sentence is reported, never removed

09_paragraph_interleave.py.why: decision 2: paragraph runs EN,ZH,EN,ZH are reordered; the stray blank stays and is reported

10_paragraph_block_form.py.why: A4: the hand-fixed block form produces 0 changes

11_one_plus_one.py.why: A2: one EN line + one ZH line is the allowed short form

12_csharp_interleaved.cs.why: C# line comments are migrated and pass the lexer check

13_ts_template_literal.ts.why: lines inside a template literal look like comments; the lexer check must stop the rewrite

14_mixed_line_split.py.why: PR #51: a line holding one EN and one ZH sentence is split at the boundary, text kept word for word

15_crlf_interleaved.py.why: PR #50: CRLF line endings are kept exactly

16_rule_line_between_paragraphs.py.why: a rule line (+===+) between paragraphs is structure: never dropped by a paragraph reorder

17_split_paragraph.py.why: docstring #1 shape: a stray blank cut EN1, whose tail shares a paragraph with ZH1; the paragraph splits, the block reorders, the stray blank stays and is reported

18_module_docstring_pairs.py.why: docstring #3 shape: module docstring EN1/ZH1/EN2/ZH2 becomes the hand-fixed form exactly

19_class_docstring_pairs.py.why: docstring #4 shape: indented class docstring EN1/ZH1/EN2/ZH2
